The Industry Brief

Edition No. 8Covering November 2 to 8, 2026Published November 9, 2026

Tesla Lets the Cybertruck Go, Toyota's Hybrid Quarter and Europe Reins In FSD

Tesla will take apart the Cybertruck line to build more Cybercabs. Toyota's profit jumped as hybrids topped half its sales and its plug-in RAV4 learned to fast-charge, Europe made Tesla rename FSD and slow it down, BMW cut its forecast while Ferrari raised its own, BYD sold 300,000 battery EVs in a month, a Chinese EV passed 500 km/h and a 106-mile F50 sold for $18.7 million.

By Margot Devries · 30 minute read

In this edition

  1. Tesla will stop building the Cybertruck to make room for the Cybercab
  2. Toyota's profit jumps 34% as hybrids top half its sales, and the plug-in RAV4 learns to charge like an EV
  3. Europe makes Tesla call FSD "Assisted Driving" and cut how far over the limit it can go
  4. BMW cuts its forecast again, and Ferrari raises its own
  5. October sales rise 3%, Mazda jumps 25% and the Ford Escape is down to 150
  6. BYD sells 300,000 battery EVs in a month, and Geely launches a hybrid that runs on methanol
  7. The first production car past 500 km/h is a Chinese EV
  8. A 106-mile Ferrari F50 sells for $18.7 million, and a Daytona SP3 nearly matches it

The week's theme was what carmakers choose to build, and what they give up to build it. Tesla is giving up a truck to make more robotaxis, Ford gave up the Escape to build an electric pickup, Ferrari keeps building fewer cars than people want, and Geely is building a car for a fuel most of the world has never used. Meanwhile, regulators in Europe showed they can change what a car's software does after it's sold. As always, every story carries a status line, because a final count, a forecast and a promise in a press release are not the same kind of news.

Electric vehicles · Tesla

Announced November 5–6 on X · production at Giga Texas ends around June or July 2027 · Tesla hasn't said whether the truck will be built anywhere else

Tesla Will Stop Building the Cybertruck to Make Room for the Cybercab

Elon Musk once predicted a quarter of a million a year. Americans bought about 20,000 last year, and the Texas line will be taken apart next summer to build more robotaxis.

AUSTIN, Texas — "Tesla will be winding down production of the Cybertruck at Gigafactory Texas around the middle of next year to make room for increased Cybercab production," Elon Musk posted on X late on November 5, Pacific time. Giga Texas is the only plant that builds the truck, and Tesla hasn't said whether it will be built anywhere else. On November 7, Musk said the order backlog was "far more than we can make before dismantling the line for Cybercab expansion around June/July next year," and that Tesla would add a shift to try to fill it. The same week, Tesla raised prices by up to $7,500 and stopped taking orders for the cheapest version, so the least expensive Cybertruck you can order is now the Premium AWD, at $92,490. Wes Morrill, the truck's lead engineer, said Tesla will keep supplying parts and service.

In October 2023, Musk said he expected "roughly 0.25 million Cybertrucks a year" by sometime in 2025, and that "over 1 million people" had reserved one. Kelley Blue Book estimates Americans bought 38,965 in 2024, 20,237 in 2025 and 11,586 in the first 9 months of this year, 28% fewer than a year earlier. The truck was promised in 2019 from $39,900 (about $52,600 in today's money) and listed in 2023 from $60,990 (about $67,400 today), and it has had 11 recalls. It never went on sale in the European Union, mainly because of pedestrian-safety rules, and last month Tesla canceled it for Australia and New Zealand.

Scale 0–250,000. Tesla doesn't report Cybertruck sales; these are Kelley Blue Book estimates. Sources: Cox Automotive and Kelley Blue Book, January 13 and October 12, 2026; Tesla's third-quarter 2023 earnings call, October 18, 2023.

Even so, it's still America's best-selling electric pickup. In the third quarter, its estimated 4,323 sales beat the Rivian R1T, the GMC Sierra EV and the Chevrolet Silverado EV, each at about 1,700. Ford ended the all-electric F-150 Lightning last December, after pausing production in October, and plans a range-extended version for 2027, and Ram canceled its battery-electric 1500 in 2025. The Cybercab, the 2-seat robotaxi that replaces the truck on the line, has carried riders in Austin since September 3, and Tesla lists its capacity in Texas at more than 125,000 a year, the same as the Cybertruck's. Morrill called the truck "an incredible technology development platform" that "lives on through Cybercab": its 48-volt electrics and steer-by-wire carried over.

The Cybercab is still under a federal audit. Tesla filed its sworn answers to NHTSA's 21 questions about how it certified the car by the October 30 deadline, but the public version is a 1-page letter that reads: "The entirety of this file is confidential business information." NHTSA hasn't ruled on whether to keep it secret.

The Carveyance take

The Cybertruck did what Tesla built it to do: everyone talked about it, and it taught Tesla things the Cybercab now uses. It never sold like a pickup. Tesla is swapping a truck people stopped buying for a car it mostly plans to run itself, and that says more about where Tesla thinks its money will come from than about trucks.

What to watch: whether the truck moves to another plant, how many orders Tesla fills before the line comes out, and NHTSA's decision on the Cybercab's sealed answers.

Earnings and hybrids · Toyota

Results November 5 · the full-year figures are Toyota's forecasts · the 2027 RAV4 Plug-in Hybrid reaches dealers early in 2027

Toyota's Profit Jumps 34% as Hybrids Top Half Its Sales, and the Plug-In RAV4 Learns to Charge Like an EV

Toyota raised its full-year forecast by ¥500 billion (about $3.2 billion) while absorbing about ¥1.1 trillion (about $7 billion) in US tariffs, and it gave every 2027 RAV4 Plug-in Hybrid a Tesla-style port and DC fast charging.

TOYOTA CITY, Japan — Toyota's operating profit for July to September rose 34% to ¥1.13 trillion (about $7.1 billion), its first increase in 6 quarters, Reuters reported. Net profit fell 18.5% to ¥759.4 billion (about $4.8 billion), because of a swing in items below the operating line. Toyota raised its operating-profit forecast for the year to March by ¥500 billion (about $3.2 billion), to ¥3.9 trillion (about $24.7 billion), even as it expects US tariffs to cost it about ¥1.1 trillion (about $7 billion) this year. North America swung back to profit for the first half, with ¥166.1 billion (about $1.05 billion) against a loss of ¥67.8 billion (about $429 million) a year earlier, which Toyota put down to "price revisions and the reduced impact of U.S. tariffs." Hybrids, plug-ins and EVs made up 55.6% of Toyota and Lexus sales in the half, up from 46.7%. The shares closed up about 17%, their biggest 1-day gain since 1987, according to Reuters. Toyota also named Mark Templin, its North American chief operating officer, to replace Ted Ogawa as chief executive of Toyota Motor North America on January 1.

PLANO, Texas — The same day, Toyota said every 2027 RAV4 Plug-in Hybrid gets a NACS port, the connector Tesla designed, along with DC fast charging and an 11 kW onboard charger. For 2026, only the XSE and Woodland could fast-charge, through a CCS port. Toyota estimates an electric range of 52 miles for the SE, 50 for the XSE, 46 for the Woodland and 45 for the GR Sport. All 4 have 321 hp and all-wheel drive, and prices start at $42,100 before destination. Toyota didn't give a maximum DC charging speed, or say whether the RAV4 can use Tesla's Superchargers.

The Carveyance take

A weaker yen did much of the work this quarter, but the sales mix shows where Toyota's strength is: hybrids, plug-ins and EVs, the cars it never stopped believing in, were more than half of what it sold. And a 50-mile plug-in hybrid that can fast-charge is something new for most American buyers: a car that can run on electricity all week, charge in public when there's no charger at home, and still drive across the country on gasoline.

What to watch: the RAV4's fast-charging speed and whether it gets Supercharger access, and whether Toyota's tariff estimate keeps falling.

Driver assistance · Tesla in Europe

Approved by the Netherlands' RDW November 3 · cars with Hardware 4 or newer · by over-the-air update, no date given · approval for the whole EU still pending

Europe Makes Tesla Call FSD "Assisted Driving" and Cut How Far Over the Limit It Can Go

The Dutch vehicle authority approved a new name and a cap of 10% over the speed limit, down from 50%. It's a rare case of a car's software being changed after it's sold, to satisfy regulators.

ZOETERMEER, Netherlands — RDW, the Dutch vehicle authority, approved changes to Tesla's driver-assistance system on November 3. "FSD Supervised" becomes "Tesla Assisted Driving" on the screen, in the owner's manual and in all driver information. The margin a driver can set above the detected speed limit falls from as much as 50% to a maximum of 10%, and it resets to 0% every time the car starts. On a highway with a 130 km/h (81 mph) limit, that means a top speed of 143 km/h (89 mph) instead of 195 km/h (121 mph). The system otherwise works the same way, RDW said, and it's still driver assistance: "The driver remains responsible for driving," as RDW put it in Dutch.

RDW approved FSD Supervised in April, the first approval in Europe, and it applied only in the Netherlands. 9 other countries have since adopted it: Belgium, Croatia, Czechia, Denmark, Estonia, Latvia, Lithuania, Slovakia and Slovenia. The changes follow an agreement Tesla reached with Germany's transport ministry, whose October statement, as translated from German, called the name "FSD" "somewhat misleading." Approval for the whole EU needs a qualified majority of member states in a technical committee whose talks RDW calls confidential, and reports point to a vote in December at the earliest. The update reaches cars with Hardware 4 or newer over the air, and RDW didn't give a date.

The Carveyance take

In America, Tesla still sells "Full Self-Driving (Supervised)." In Europe, under pressure from regulators, Tesla has made the name match what the system does: help for a driver who stays in charge. And cars already on the road will behave differently, through a software update. Software lets a carmaker improve a car overnight, and it lets regulators get one changed overnight, too.

What to watch: the EU committee vote, and whether the new name and the 10% cap spread beyond Europe.

Earnings · BMW and Ferrari

Ferrari's results November 3 · BMW cut its forecast November 3 and reported November 4 · forecasts are company guidance

BMW Cuts Its Forecast Again, and Ferrari Raises Its Own

BMW now expects its car business to earn roughly nothing this year after its China sales fell by a quarter. Ferrari shipped 33 fewer cars and made 13% more money.

MUNICH — BMW cut its outlook for the second time in less than 5 months on the evening of November 3. It now expects an EBIT margin of between −0.5% and +0.5% for its car business this year, down from 1% to 3%, and from 4% to 6% when the year began. Before restructuring costs, it still expects more than 2%. In the third quarter, its deliveries fell 6.3% to 551,075, revenue fell 5.8% to €30.45 billion (about $34.1 billion) and net profit fell 14.7% to €1.45 billion (about $1.62 billion). The damage is concentrated in one place: deliveries in China fell 24.8% to 114,355, while the US rose 2.5% and Europe 2.6%. The new charges, booked in the fourth quarter, come from extending a voluntary job-cut program for about 8,000 people, announced in July, that filled within about 3 weeks of opening in October, and cutting management faster than planned. "Current developments in our industry call for decisiveness and swift implementation," said Milan Nedeljković, who became chief executive in May.

MARANELLO, Italy — Ferrari shipped 3,368 cars in the same quarter, 33 fewer than a year earlier, and still raised revenue 7% to €1.90 billion (about $2.12 billion) and net profit 13% to €431 million (about $483 million). Its shipments to mainland China, Hong Kong and Taiwan fell from 248 to 143, which it blamed on a model changeover. Personalization, the paint, trim and carbon fiber buyers add to each car, passed 21% of its revenue from cars and spare parts, its finance chief said, and Ferrari raised its 2026 forecast for the second time, to about €7.65 billion (about $8.57 billion) in revenue. "Our order book now reaches into 2028," said Benedetto Vigna, the chief executive. Ferrari's first electric car, the Luce, reaches its first customers this quarter, and Vigna said the Luce's 2027 deliveries are "fully allocated."

BMW wasn't the only one hurting. Volvo Cars, which now reports sales in rolling 3-month periods, sold 141,656 cars from August through October, 16% fewer than a year earlier. Its electric car sales rose 27%, but plug-in hybrids fell 30% and everything else fell 28%. "In China, we are adapting to lower demand and focusing on stabilizing the business rather than chasing volumes," said Erik Severinson, its chief commercial officer.

The Carveyance take

The luxury car business is splitting by price. At the very top, buyers keep paying more for fewer cars, and Ferrari keeps raising its forecast by selling options alongside cars. Just below it, the premium brands that grew up on Chinese demand are cutting jobs and models. BMW's sales are rising in America and Europe; its problem is that China was where the money was.

What to watch: the size of BMW's fourth-quarter restructuring charge, the long-wheelbase iX3's launch in China this month, and how the market receives Ferrari's Luce.

Sales · October in America

Reported November 3–4 · GM, Stellantis and Tesla report only quarterly, so every total includes estimates · October had 1 more selling day than a year earlier

October Sales Rise 3%, Mazda Jumps 25% and the Ford Escape Is Down to 150

An extra selling day flattered the total, and the underlying pace slowed. Kia and Hyundai had their best Octobers ever, and Ford's sales grew about 7% once you leave out the 2 models it stopped building.

ATLANTA — Cox Automotive estimates Americans bought about 1,324,000 new vehicles in October, up 2.9%. But October had 28 selling days this year against 27 a year ago, so sales per day actually fell 0.8%, and the seasonally adjusted pace slowed to 15.5 million a year, the slowest since January, Cox said. Other estimates run as high as 4%, because GM, Stellantis and Tesla report sales only once a quarter. Through October, sales are down about 1.5% for the year.

Mazda sold 31,446, up 25%, mostly on the CX-90, the Mazda3 and the CX-70; the CX-50 slipped 1.2%. Kia sold 80,008, up 16%, its sixth record month in a row, with the new Telluride up 63%. Hyundai had its best October ever, and Honda sold an October-record 32,519 hybrids. Ford's total fell 0.8% to 174,123, though F-Series pickups rose 8.2% and the Explorer 35%. The difference was the Escape, which sold 150 against 10,689 a year earlier, and the Lincoln Corsair, which sold none. Ford stopped building both at its Louisville plant in December 2025, so the plant could be retooled for the Fathom, its $28,350 electric pickup. Without them, Ford's sales rose about 7%. Ford's own stock report shows about 400 Escapes left on dealer lots.

The Carveyance take

The headline rose because the month was longer. The brands that grew the most are the ones with hybrids to sell and fresh 3-row SUVs, and the clearest sign of change is the Escape: a car that sold more than 300,000 a year at its peak, retired so its plant could build an electric pickup.

What to watch: Kelley Blue Book's October transaction prices, due mid-month, and whether the slower pace carries into November.

China · BYD and Geely

BYD's sales November 1 · Geely's launch November 3 · market figures from the China Passenger Car Association, November 9 · ranges and efficiency are Geely's claims, on China's CLTC test

BYD Sells 300,000 Battery EVs in a Month, and Geely Launches a Hybrid That Runs on Methanol

2 of China's biggest carmakers are pulling in different directions: BYD toward batteries and exports, Geely toward a fuel most of the world has never put in a car. At home, the market keeps shrinking.

SHENZHEN, China — BYD sold 490,168 cars and commercial vehicles in October, up 11% and its best month this year. Its battery-electric passenger cars rose 37% to 305,743, its first month above 300,000, while plug-in hybrids fell 17% to 177,382. Sales outside China doubled to 170,194, about 35% of the total. BYD is still down 2.2% for the year, at 3.62 million, and to beat last year's 4.6 million it needs about 490,000 a month in November and December. China's own market is shrinking: retail sales of passenger cars fell 27.1% in October to 1.64 million, the China Passenger Car Association said, though electric cars and plug-ins took a record 67.5% of them. The purchase tax on those cars went from zero to 5% on January 1, and trade-in subsidies are now a percentage of the price. "Funding remains available for trade-in subsidies, but their marginal impact is diminishing," the association said. Exports are filling the gap: China's exports of electric cars and plug-ins rose 145% to 582,000.

SHENYANG, China — On November 3, Geely launched the Galaxy Xingyao 6 EF, a plug-in hybrid sedan whose 1.5-liter engine runs on methanol, gasoline or any mix of the 2 in the same tank. Geely calls it the world's first production methanol hybrid family car, although it launched a methanol hybrid Emgrand in 2022. It goes 130 or 230 km (81 or 143 miles) on electricity, depending on the battery, and about 1,250 km (777 miles) in all with a full battery and a tank of methanol, against 1,880 km (1,168 miles) on gasoline, because methanol carries about half the energy of gasoline per gallon. Geely claims 48.15% thermal efficiency for the engine, and introductory prices start at 76,800 yuan (about $11,500). It says China has more than 1,400 methanol stations; the Methanol Institute counted about 500 in 2025.

The Carveyance take

BYD shows where most of China's car industry is heading: battery cars, built in enormous numbers and increasingly sold abroad. Geely's methanol hybrid is a hedge for cold regions, long distances and places without chargers. Its climate case depends entirely on how the methanol is made, and most of China's has been made from coal.

What to watch: BYD's November figures against its 2025 total, the China Association of Automobile Manufacturers' October data, and whether Geely sells a methanol car outside China.

Enthusiasts · Yangwang

Run November 1 in Abu Dhabi · reviewed by the FIA and listed by Guinness · a 1-way run, not a 2-way average · 30 cars to be built

The First Production Car Past 500 km/h Is a Chinese EV

BYD's Yangwang U9 Xtreme hit 503.17 km/h (312.7 mph) on a closed highway in Abu Dhabi. It ran in 1 direction only, which is why the traditional 2-way record still belongs to SSC.

ABU DHABI — On November 1, the German racing driver Marc Basseng drove a Yangwang U9 Xtreme to 503.17 km/h (312.7 mph) on a closed 10 km stretch of the E11 highway in the Al Dhafra region, 6.95 km/h faster than a U9 Xtreme managed at the Papenburg test track in Germany in September 2025. Guinness World Records lists it as the highest speed reached by a production car in a single-direction run, measured with the car's speedometer and a calibrated VBOX and reviewed by an FIA representative. Guinness itself says the record "should not be confused with conventional fastest-production-car records, which require different testing protocols, including runs in opposite directions."

The U9 Xtreme has 4 electric motors of up to 555 kW each, 2,220 kW in all (about 2,977 hp), a 1,200-volt system and a Blade battery that can deliver up to 1,800 kW. It ran on semi-slick tires developed with Giti. BYD will build 30, and cars sold at April's Beijing auto show went for more than 20 million yuan (about $3 million) each. The 2-way record, the average of runs in opposite directions, is still the SSC Tuatara's 455.3 km/h (282.9 mph), set in Florida in January 2021. Bugatti's Chiron Super Sport 300+ prototype went 490.48 km/h (304.77 mph) in 1 direction in 2019, then Bugatti stopped chasing top speed.

The Carveyance take

A 1-way run on a highway isn't the same as a 2-way average, and even Guinness says so. But 503 km/h is 503 km/h, and the car that did it is electric, Chinese and, in principle, for sale. 10 years ago, all 3 of those would have sounded unlikely.

What to watch: whether BYD tries a 2-way run, and whether Bugatti, Koenigsegg or Rimac answers.

Collector cars · Auctions

Sales held October 31 · prices include the buyer's premium · the "records" are the auction houses' own claims

A 106-Mile Ferrari F50 Sells for $18.7 Million, and a Daytona SP3 Nearly Matches It

2 sales on the same day set records on both sides of the Atlantic. The money went to rare, barely driven modern Ferraris, not to the collector market as a whole.

LAS VEGAS — Broad Arrow's auction at the Wynn on October 31 brought $92.8 million, which the company, owned by Hagerty, calls the highest total ever for a collector-car auction in Las Vegas. Its first sale there, a year earlier, made $13.7 million. 64 of the 84 cars sold. A 1997 F50, the 334th of 349 built, delivered new in Britain and driven 106 miles, sold for $18,705,000. That's $4.13 million above the previous F50 record of $14,575,000, set at Mecum's Monterey sale in August, though still short of its pre-sale estimate of more than $20 million. An F50 cost about $475,000 new in America in 1995, about $1.05 million in today's money.

A 2025 Daytona SP3 with 81 miles, sold by its first owner, made $18,540,000, a record for an SP3 not sold for charity and about 8 times its launch price of €2 million, or $2.26 million in 2021 (about $2.8 million today). With a LaFerrari at $8,805,000, those 3 cars made about half the sale's total. In London the same day, RM Sotheby's sale made £36.55 million (about $48.6 million), which it calls the highest total for a collector-car auction in Britain. Its own Daytona SP3, a former factory development car with 2,948 miles, brought £8.16 million (about $10.9 million), about $7.7 million less than the Las Vegas car.

The rest of the market isn't moving with them. Hagerty's Market Rating was 58.73 in September, "essentially flat," after hitting its lowest level in nearly 15 years in January, when Hagerty said "values are down across the board." At Monterey in August, it found cars from the 1950s and 1960s selling below their condition values on average, while cars from the 1980s to the 2020s sold at premiums of 31% to 38%.

The Carveyance take

These are records for a handful of nearly new, nearly unused Ferraris, bought by people for whom $18 million is a fair price for a car they'll barely drive. The wider collector market is flat. If your old Porsche didn't double in value this year, you're in the majority.

What to watch: whether the F50 run continues at January's sales in Florida and Arizona, and Hagerty's October market rating.

Safety Notices

5 recalls reported this week. Repairs are free, and you can check any car by its VIN at nhtsa.gov/recalls.

GM EVs: brakes can briefly let go
67,380 vehicles: the 2023–2027 Cadillac Lyriq, 2025–2026 Celestiq, 2026–2027 Vistiq and 2024–2027 Chevrolet Blazer EV, with the Lyriq and Blazer EV covered only in their performance all-wheel-drive versions. If the brakes are lightly applied in a sharp, low-speed turn and a wheel hits a bump or dip, such as the end of a driveway, the brake software can misread the wheel's movement and briefly release the brakes. They return on the next press of the pedal. GM has 24 complaints, including 20 minor crashes. It's the second brake-software recall for the Lyriq; the 2024 fix missed this case. The update is over the air or at a dealer, and owner letters go out December 14. NHTSA campaign 26V717.
Hyundai Kona Electric and Veloster N: airbags can switch off
37,901 vehicles: 29,058 Kona Electrics from the 2019–2023 model years and 8,843 Veloster Ns from 2019–2022. If the airbag control unit loses power or reboots while it's saving data, the data can be corrupted, the airbag light comes on and the airbags and seat-belt pretensioners may not work. Hyundai has 331 reports and no known injuries in America. Dealers will update the software, and owner letters go out January 1. NHTSA campaign 26V728.
Lincoln Navigator: a seat that moves on its own
36,994 Navigators from the 2025–2027 model years. A fault in the rear audio controls can trigger the "chauffeur" feature and move or recline the front passenger seat without anyone asking. Dealers will update the software and disable chauffeur mode. NHTSA campaign 26V691.
Ford F-150 and Super Duty: tailgate cables
30,123 trucks: F-150s from the 2026–2027 model years and Super Duty pickups from 2026. The left tailgate cable can fail under a heavy load. The fix is expected in January. NHTSA campaign 26V689.
Chevrolet Express and GMC Savana: steering
12,715 vans from the 2025–2026 model years. A nut in the steering gear may not have been tightened properly and can come loose, causing a loss of steering control. Dealers will check the steering gear's serial number and replace it if needed; vans not properly inspected under an earlier recall must be checked again. Owner letters go out December 14. NHTSA campaign 26V718.

Also That Week

6 more stories worth knowing, in brief.

Formula 1 · Mercedes

Clinched November 1 at the Mexico City Grand Prix

Kimi Antonelli Becomes F1's Youngest Champion

MEXICO CITY — Kimi Antonelli clinched the 2026 world championship for Mercedes by finishing third in Mexico City on November 1, at 20 years and 68 days old. That beats Sebastian Vettel's record of 23 years and 134 days, set in 2010. He's the first Italian champion since Alberto Ascari in 1953. "This is a moment that I will remember for the rest of my life," he said.

Why it matters: he's the first champion from Mercedes' junior program, and it's the team's first drivers' title since 2020.

Formula 1 · Obituary

Died November 5

Alan Jones, Williams' First World Champion, Dies at 80

MELBOURNE, Australia — Alan Jones, the 1980 world champion, died on November 5, 3 days after his 80th birthday, after a short illness, his wife said. He won 12 Grands Prix, 11 of them for Williams, and gave the team its first drivers' title in only its fourth season. Stefano Domenicali, F1's chief executive, called him "a true great of our sport and an extraordinary racer."

Why it matters: Williams' first title started one of F1's great teams.

NASCAR · Dodge

Announced November 2 at SEMA · drivers named November 6 · racing from Daytona in February

Dodge Returns to NASCAR's Cup Series

LAS VEGAS — Dodge will race in the Cup Series in 2027 for the first time since 2012, the year it won the title with Brad Keselowski. Kaulig Racing will run the cars, with AJ Allmendinger in the No. 16 and Ty Dillon in the No. 10. The car, expected to be a Charger, is due to be shown in December. "Everyone said it was impossible to get back in one year," said Tim Kuniskis, who runs Stellantis's American brands and SRT.

Why it matters: Dodge becomes the Cup Series' fourth manufacturer, alongside Chevrolet, Ford and Toyota.

Aftermarket · SEMA

Shown November 3–6 in Las Vegas · most are concepts, not for sale

SEMA's Concepts Bring Back Manuals, V8s and a Wrangler Pickup

LAS VEGAS — Jeep showed the Wrangler Scrambler SRT Concept, a 2-door Wrangler pickup with "V8 power" and the first independent front suspension on a Wrangler. Ford's Bronco Frostwarden, a one-off, uses the supercharged 7.3-liter Megazilla 2.0 crate engine, rated at more than 1,200 hp on race fuel. Nissan showed a Sentra Spec-V Concept with a turbocharged 2.0-liter and a 6-speed manual, and Honda said the Civic Type R HRC Concept is "in development for the U.S. market." Direct Connection, Stellantis's performance-parts brand, announced a $10,995 supercharger kit that takes the Ram 1500 Rumble Bee SRT to "up to 900 hp."

Why it matters: the concepts carmakers bring to an enthusiast show say what they think enthusiasts want, and this year it was manuals, V8s and trucks.

Fuel economy · Regulation

Court filing November 2 · the rule takes effect November 30 · a legal challenge is pending

Carmakers Defend the New Fuel-Economy Rule in Court

BOSTON — The Alliance for Automotive Innovation, whose members include GM, Ford, Toyota, Hyundai, Stellantis and Volkswagen, filed in support of the government's revised fuel-economy standards at the US Court of Appeals for the 1st Circuit, where California, Michigan and about 2 dozen other states and local governments are challenging them. The rule sets a fleetwide target of about 34.9 mpg for 2031, against about 50.4 mpg under the 2024 rule, by that rule's own estimate. The government estimates it cuts the cost of a 2031 vehicle by $1,289 on average and raises US gasoline use by 4.6% through 2050.

Why it matters: the target decides how hard carmakers have to push hybrids and EVs in America over the next 5 years.

Car culture · Disneyland

Reported November 2 · gas cars retire by early 2027

Disneyland's Autopia Goes Electric After 71 Years

ANAHEIM, Calif. — Autopia, the ride that has given children their first turn at a steering wheel since Disneyland opened in 1955, is retiring its gasoline cars, The New York Times reported. In 2024, the California Air Resources Board found the cars' engines lacked proper emissions certification, and Disney paid a $56,250 settlement. The cars now run 8.5 hp Honda engines, up to 16 hours a day, and the gas fleet is due to retire by early 2027.

Why it matters: for a lot of Americans, Autopia was the first car they ever drove.

Since Last Week

Where last week's stories went next.

Follow-up · The Canada tariff

There's still no deal. "We have the concept of a very good deal with Canada," President Trump said on November 1, and on November 3 Prime Minister Mark Carney said: "They're asking less and they're offering more but we're not quite there." The 50% tariff on Canadian-built cars that Trump announced in August is still set for January 1, though The Auto Wire reported that it could find no formal document setting that rate. The 2 leaders are expected to meet at the APEC summit in Shenzhen, China, on November 18 and 19. Read last week's story

Follow-up · Audi in Georgia

Last week, Audi was promised talks on tariff relief. This week, documents released by a Georgia development authority showed Audi is considering a second, $3 billion phase for its planned plant in Peach County, adding 3,000 jobs by 2033 to the first phase's $4 billion, 4,500 jobs and up to 200,000 SUVs a year, Reuters and The Atlanta Journal-Constitution reported. Audi declined to comment. Read last week's Brief

Follow-up · Fuel prices

Regular gasoline averaged $4.01 a gallon on November 9, AAA said, down from $4.17 a week earlier and $4.37 a month ago, but still 94 cents more than a year ago. AAA says the national average had never been above $4 in November before this year.

Worth Watching

Not big stories yet, but they could be.

Nissan's results, November 11
Nissan reports its first-half results on Wednesday. Its shares hit a 52-week low on October 27.
Britain's EV target
The Guardian reported that the government is expected to cut the share of new cars that must be zero-emission in 2030 from 80% to about 60%. The government says "no decisions have been taken." A decision could come this week.
Waymo and school buses
On November 9, NHTSA opened a recall query into 2,895 Waymo vehicles to check whether the software recall Waymo issued last December, after its cars passed stopped school buses, actually fixed the problem. TechCrunch reported that most of the reported passes came after the fix.
China's October total
The China Association of Automobile Manufacturers usually publishes its monthly figures around the 10th to the 12th, including exports, which are carrying China's carmakers this year.

News Versus Noise

How solid is each story? Our ledger for the week.

Confirmed
Musk's post on ending Cybertruck production in Texas, and Tesla's new prices. Toyota's results and forecast, and the 2027 RAV4 Plug-in Hybrid's charging. RDW's approval of Tesla Assisted Driving. The results from BMW, Ferrari and Volvo Cars. October sales from the carmakers that report monthly. BYD's, Geely's and the China Passenger Car Association's October figures. The U9 Xtreme's 503.17 km/h, as listed by Guinness. The auction results. The 5 recalls.
Reported, not confirmed
Audi's second phase in Georgia, from development-authority documents; Audi declined to comment. Musk's November 9 post saying Tesla will have to return many Cybertruck deposits, seen so far only in secondary reports. Ford Authority's report of a compact electric crossover for Louisville in 2029.
Plans without dates
When the RDW-approved changes reach Teslas. Whether the Cybertruck moves to another plant. The range-extended F-150 Lightning, due in 2027. Geely's plans for methanol cars outside China.
Not final yet
Approval of Tesla Assisted Driving for the whole EU. A US–Canada deal, and the 50% tariff it would replace. The court case over the fuel-economy rule. Britain's 2030 EV target. BMW's restructuring charge.
Noise
"The world's first methanol hybrid": Geely launched a methanol hybrid Emgrand in 2022. "The world's fastest production car": the U9 Xtreme's record is for a single direction, and the 2-way record is still SSC's. Reports that the RAV4 Plug-in Hybrid can use Tesla's Superchargers: Toyota hasn't said so. Footage said to show a U9 Xtreme test car crashing: unverified. And the 18.6% hybrid share some outlets reported for October: that was J.D. Power's forecast, not a result.
